title: Soup Making
strapline: A pot of chopped veg simmered down to something warm — cooking that fills the whole room with smell.
intent: Making soup lets children watch hard, solid vegetables soften and change in the pot, and taste that heat transforms food.
Washing, peeling and chopping vegetables is a rich sequence of hand skills with a real, shared purpose at the end.
Choosing, sorting and counting vegetables into the pot weaves number, classification and vocabulary through genuine work.
Soup is deeply communal — everyone chops, everyone stirs, everyone tastes — so it builds belonging and cooperation.
Cooking soup from vegetables children helped grow or shop for closes a loop from soil to bowl that they remember.
Meeting the soups of many families and seasons widens what children are willing to taste and talk about.
implementation: Give every child a real job — scrubbing, peeling with a child-safe peeler, chopping soft veg with a table knife — and rotate across the recipe.
Narrate the change as it happens: 'the carrot was so hard, feel it now — what did the heat do?'
Count and name vegetables into the pot together, and sort them first by colour or kind.
Cook down real vegetables in a slow cooker or on a supervised hob, letting the smell build anticipation across the morning.
Bring in family soup recipes, ideally cooked alongside the children by the family who make them.
Serve the soup together at snack with bread the bakers made, and let the room taste what the cooking group produced.
key_questions: The carrot was so hard — feel it now. What did the heat do?
How many vegetables shall we chop for the pot?
Can we sort these by colour before they go in?
What can you smell as the soup cooks?
Where did our vegetables come from — do you remember?

impact.text: Children watch hard vegetables soften and change, tasting that heat transforms food.
Children wash, peel and chop — a rich sequence of hand skills with a real, shared purpose.
Children choose, sort and count vegetables into the pot, weaving number and classification through the work.
Children build belonging and cooperation — everyone chops, stirs and tastes.
Children meet the soups of many families and seasons, widening what they'll taste.

enhancements: A real job for every child — scrubbing, peeling, chopping soft veg — rotated across the recipe.
A slow cooker or supervised hob so the smell builds anticipation across the morning.
Family soup recipes cooked alongside the children where possible.
A sort-by-colour-or-kind step before the vegetables go in.
Soup served with the bakers' bread so the room tastes what the group made.

playing_exploring: Children handle, smell and taste real vegetables and test what their hands and tools can do to them.
Peeling and chopping are satisfying, absorbing jobs with a visible pile of results.
active_learning: A pot of soup is a long project with a warm finish, and children hold the goal through the chopping, the simmer and the wait.
creating_thinking: Children predict what heat will do to a hard carrot, then meet the soft, changed reality in the pot.
